meta.title: Genki Ikeda | Software Engineer
meta.description: Software engineer who runs development — from requirements to implementation, review, and merge — on a self-built autonomous development system. Founder of 0ai Inc.

name: Genki Ikeda
tagline: I build the system that lets AI agents do the development, and run everything from clarifying requirements to design, implementation, review, and merge on it.
about: I have worked on full-stack web and cloud development since 2019. Working mostly with startups and nonprofits, I have often built the frontend, backend, and infrastructure of new products on my own.

Since 2024 I have focused on building products with generative AI. I led generative AI products as CTO and tech lead at a startup, and since October 2025 I have worked as a contract AI engineer at a SaaS company serving the pharmaceutical industry. In January 2026 I founded 0ai Inc., where I build products in which AI agents carry out business operations on their own.

I also hand my own development over to an autonomous development system I built. People focus on goals and judgment calls; agents handle the repetitive work of implementing, verifying, and merging. That is how I work every day.

system.lead: A development platform in which agents follow defined procedures from clarifying requirements all the way to merging and cleaning up. The procedures and decision rules are kept independent of the agent runtime, so the same workflow runs on both Claude Code and Codex.

steps.title: Requirements and design
steps.body: Goals and acceptance criteria are settled through dialogue. Important decisions are challenged by a separate reviewer agent that has no access to the conversation that produced them.

steps.title: Implementation
steps.body: Each piece of work automatically gets its own issue, pull request, and isolated worktree, so several tasks can be implemented in parallel.

steps.title: Verification
steps.body: Besides tests, a reviewer agent without the authoring context checks the result against the acceptance criteria. Anything where appearance matters is checked in a real rendering.

steps.title: Merge and cleanup
steps.body: Merging, cleaning up branches and worktrees, and updating issues and project status are all automated.

steps.title: Accumulated knowledge
steps.body: The reasons and background behind decisions are saved as memories and recalled in later work. Failures feed back into fixing the procedures themselves.

steps.title: Always-on operation
steps.body: Resident processes pick up requests from Slack and scheduled tasks, and notify me only when a decision needs a human.

highlights.title: Implementation is delegated
highlights.body: I rarely drive the terminal (TUI) myself to implement anything.

highlights.title: So is upstream communication
highlights.body: The upstream communication that development needs — talking with teammates, confirming specifications — is handled by AI as well. The only part I do myself is attending the actual meetings.

highlights.title: A closed context
highlights.body: Meeting content is handed to the AI too, so work moves forward with every piece of context the job needs already in the AI's hands.

As product owner, led requirements, the roadmap, and task management for a team of three.

Developed a robo-advisor web app: support for Japan's new NISA tax-free investment program, a large refactoring of the recurring investment settings, and public identity verification with the My Number Card.

Set up a serverless architecture with infrastructure as code, CI/CD, automated integration tests, and Slack alerts on failure, keeping it running with little operational effort.
Worked on requirements and specifications for a super app that brings car-related services into one app, and implemented web view integration and push notification control.
Built a new e-commerce site and a review app from scratch, including a lottery sales system for popular items, localization and SEO, and the iOS and Android releases.
Improved an FX trading system, implementing role-based access control and localization.
Developed web and mobile apps for parents of students at an online tutoring school, building more than ten screens and reviewing team members' code.
Built an in-house RPA tool and a web console that runs it remotely, covering everything from requirements to testing, and prototyped an image-processing model.
